ENFORCEMENT DECREE OF THE NAKDONG RIVER BASIN WATER MANAGEMENT AND RESIDENT SUPPORT ACT

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Nakdong River Basin Water Management and Resident Support Act and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Types of Basic Environmental Facilities)
"Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 4 (f) of Article 2 of the Nakdong River Basin Water Management and Resident Support Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following facilities installed and operated by the State or a local government: <Amended on June 30, 2009; Nov. 16, 2011; Jan. 28, 2014; Jan. 16, 2018>
1. Buffer storage facilities capable of holding for a certain period sewage, wastewater, etc. discharged from industrial complexes under subparagraph 8 (a) through (d) of Article 2 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act (hereinafter referred to as "industrial complexes") and industrial areas under Article 36 (1) 1 (c) of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act (hereinafter referred to as "industrial areas");
2. Nonpoint pollution reduction facilities under subparagraph 13 of Article 2 of the Water Environment Conservation Act;
3. Artificial islands for cultivating aquatic plants, underwater air supply devices, algae removal equipment, algae reduction devices, and other facilities to prevent water pollution in rivers and lakes.

Article 3 (Scope of Designation of Riparian Zones)
(1) "Areas within a distance prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (1) of the Act means areas within the following distances from the relevant dam [measured from the design flood level line or, where there is no such line, the normal full water level line; hereinafter the same shall apply]. In such cases, the distance shall be measured upstream along the centerline of the river, lake, or equivalent body of water (hereinafter referred to as the "flow-path distance"). <Amended on July 21, 2020>
1. For a dam whose stored water is used as a regional water supply source under subparagraph 3 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act: 20 kilometers from the dam;
2. For a dam whose stored water is used for a local water supply system under subparagraph 8 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act: 10 kilometers from the dam.
(2) The river boundary under the main sentence of Article 4 (2) of the Act shall be the boundary of the river area under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the River Act and shall be determined through an on-site survey, etc. of the relevant boundary line as follows:
1. For a river for which a management register for river facilities under Article 15 of the River Act (hereinafter referred to as the "management register") has been prepared and is kept: The boundary line of the river area recorded in the management register;
2. For a river for which a management register has not been prepared and is not kept:
(a) For a river with an embankment: The boundary line of the embankment;
(b) For a river without an embankment: The boundary line of the river area on a topographic map produced by the National Geographic Information Institute.

Article 4 (Areas Excluded from Riparian Zones)
(1) "Areas prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 6 of the Act means natural settlement districts under Article 31 (2) 7 (a) of the Enforcement Decree of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act. <Amended on July 28, 2026>
(2) "Areas meeting the criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4 (2) 7 of the Act means areas in which a naturally formed village consisting of at least five households exists (excluding areas in which a naturally formed village consisting of at least five but no more than nine households exists and all owners of land and buildings in the area consent to designation as a riparian zone).

Article 4-2 (Cancellation of Designation of Riparian Zones)
(1) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment intends to cancel designation of a riparian zone under the main clause of the main sentence of Article 4 (3) of the Act, the Minister shall hear the opinion of the Nakdong River Basin Management Committee under Article 37 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee"). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(2) Before hearing the Committee's opinion under paragraph (1), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall organize a survey team composed of officials of relevant central administrative agencies and the relevant local governments, experts, resident representatives, etc. and investigate actual conditions on site. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) Where necessary when cancelling designation of a riparian zone, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may request the head of the competent local government to provide the following materials: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. The location and size of the area to be released from designation;
2. Topographic drawings showing the riparian zone before and after cancellation;
3. Other materials that the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment deems necessary.

Article 5 (Procedures and Timing for Formulating Master Plans for Management of Riparian Zones)
(1) Where formulating a master plan for management of riparian zones under Article 4-2 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "management master plan"), the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall hear the opinions of relevant local governments and request deliberation by the Committee by August 31 of the year immediately preceding the year in which the management master plan is to be formulated. <Amended on July 28, 2014; Oct. 1, 2025>
(2) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment intends to amend a management master plan formulated under paragraph (1), the Minister shall hear the opinions of relevant local governments and request deliberation by the Committee; provided, this shall not apply where the Minister intends to amend minor matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment has formulated or amended a management master plan under paragraphs (1) and (2), the Minister shall notify the relevant local governments thereof. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 5-2 (Formulation and Implementation of Implementation Plans for Riparian Ecological Belts)
(1) "Matters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 4-3 (1) 4 of the Act means the following:
1. Current use of the target area;
2. Methods of purchasing the target area;
3. Management measures after development and analysis of project effects;
4. Required financial resources and investment plans.
(2) "Cases where minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree are amended" in the proviso of Article 4-3 (3) of the Act means any of the following:
1. Where the original size of the target area is changed by no more than 30 percent;
2. Where the development period is changed by no more than six months;
3. Where the originally required financial resources are changed by no more than 30 percent.
(3) Pursuant to Article 4-3 (4) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall formulate an implementation plan for a riparian ecological belt under the main sentence of paragraph (1) of that Article (hereinafter referred to as a "riparian ecological belt implementation plan") and request deliberation by the Committee by August 31 of the year immediately preceding the year in which the riparian ecological belt development project is to be implemented. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(4) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment has formulated a riparian ecological belt implementation plan under paragraph (3), the Minister shall notify the relevant local governments thereof. The same shall apply where a formulated riparian ecological belt implementation plan is amended. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 5-3 (Scope of Manufacturing Businesses Excluded from Facilities Subject to Restrictions on Activities)
"Manufacturing businesses prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as agricultural product processing businesses" in Article 5 (1) 8 of the Act means the manufacturing businesses specified in attached Table 1.

Article 6 (Procedures for Permission for Activities in Riparian Zones)
A person who intends to obtain permission to install a facility under Article 5 (2) of the Act shall submit an application for permission to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, attaching the following documents: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Installation specifications including the area, structure, etc. of the facility to be installed;
2. Specifications stating the types and number of livestock and the method of treating livestock excreta (to be attached only where intending to install a facility under Article 5 (2) 2 of the Act);
3. Installation specifications and drawings for a sewage treatment facility under Article 24 (2) 1 (a) of the Enforcement Decree of the Sewerage Act (to be attached only where intending to install a facility under Article 5 (2) 3 of the Act).

Article 6-2 (Changes to Specific-Use Areas and Districts)
"Special grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the proviso of Article 5 (3) of the Act means cases where expansion of any of the following facilities is necessary (limited to an expansion not exceeding 30 percent of the original facility area):
1. Excreta treatment facilities under subparagraph 11 of Article 2 of the Sewerage Act;
2. Public treatment facilities under subparagraph 9 of Article 2 of the Act on the Management and Use of Livestock Excreta.

Article 7 (Scope of Areas Adjacent to Rivers)
(1) "Areas within a distance prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main sentence of Article 6 (3) of the Act means areas within the distances specified in the following subparagraphs. In such cases, the distance shall be the shortest distance by which pollutants can travel from the site of the project, etc. subject to approval, permission, etc. to the boundary of the mainstream of the Nakdong River or a tributary flowing directly into it; where its flow-path distance can be calculated, that flow-path distance shall be used. <Amended on July 28, 2014>
1. Mainstream of the Nakdong River: One kilometer from the boundary of the mainstream of the Nakdong River;
2. Tributaries flowing directly into the mainstream of the Nakdong River (limited to national or local rivers): 500 meters from the boundary of the tributary flowing directly into the mainstream of the Nakdong River.
(2) Article 3 (2) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the boundaries of the mainstream of the Nakdong River and tributaries flowing directly into it under paragraph (1).

Article 8 (Scope of Buildings and Other Facilities Required to Install Green Spaces, etc.)
"Buildings and other facilities of at least a size prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 6 (3) 4 of the Act means buildings and other facilities falling under either of the following subparagraphs whose project plan area falls under attached Table 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act: <Amended on May 9, 2014; July 28, 2014; Jan. 16, 2018>
1. Class I through Class III business places under attached Table 13 of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Environment Conservation Act;
2. Facilities falling under any subparagraph of Article 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Seoul Metropolitan Area Readjustment Planning Act.

Article 9 (Water Quality Standards)
"Standards prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 7 (1) of the Act means the following standards: <Amended on July 12, 2016>
1. For rivers: A biochemical oxygen demand of no more than one milligram per liter;
2. For lakes: Total organic carbon of no more than two milligrams per liter.

Article 10 (Procedures for Public Notice of Water Source Protection Areas)
Article 11 (2) through (4) of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to public notice of water source protection areas under Article 7 (3) of the Act. In such cases, "Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment" shall be construed as "Metropolitan City Mayor or Do Governor." <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 11 (Procedures for Purchase of Land, etc.)
(1) A person who intends to sell land and facilities attached to that land (hereinafter referred to as "land, etc.") to the State under Article 8 (1) of the Act shall submit the following documents (including electronic documents) to the head of the river basin environmental office or regional environmental office: <Amended on May 4, 2010; Nov. 2, 2010; July 28, 2014>
1. Deleted. <Nov. 2, 2010>
2. Documents concerning the current use of the land;
3. Documents describing structures, etc. on the land to be sold.
(2) Upon receiving an application for purchase of land, etc. under paragraph (1), the head of the river basin environmental office or regional environmental office shall verify the following documents through joint use of administrative information under Article 36 (1) of the Electronic Government Act; provided, where the applicant does not consent to verification under subparagraph 1, the applicant shall be required to submit the document: <Added on Nov. 2, 2010; Amended on Jan. 8, 2019>
1. For an individual, an extract of the resident registration record including the resident registration number;
2. For a corporation, a certificate of registered corporate matters;
3. A certified copy of the register for the land, etc. the applicant intends to sell.
(3) Upon receiving an application for purchase of land, etc. under paragraph (1), the head of the river basin environmental office or regional environmental office shall determine purchase priority according to the Committee's criteria for purchase priority, taking into account the characteristics of the Nakdong River basin, including distance from the river boundary and the degree of pollutant load, and shall notify the owner of the land, etc. of its purchase priority. <Amended on Nov. 2, 2010>
(4) Deleted. <July 28, 2014>
(5) Where purchasing land, etc. in an area falling under any subparagraph of Article 8 (2) of the Act, the head of the river basin environmental office or regional environmental office may give priority to its purchase following deliberation by the Committee. <Amended on July 28, 2014>

Article 11-2 (Calculation of Purchase Prices of Land, etc.)
(1) The purchase price of land, etc. under the main clause of the main sentence of Article 8 (2) of the Act shall be calculated as the arithmetic mean of values appraised under that main clause by at least two appraisal corporations, etc. under subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Act on Appraisal and Certified Appraisers. <Amended on Aug. 31, 2016; Mar. 9, 2021>
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), in any of the following cases, the purchase price may be determined on the basis of compensation for losses of land, business, etc. under the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects:
1. Where Article 8 (2) 1 of the Act applies;
2. Where all land, etc. jointly offered for sale by multiple persons is purchased and meets both of the following requirements:
(a) It shall consist of at least two adjoining parcels of land, etc. with different owners;
(b) At least 50 percent of each adjoining parcel of land, etc. shall lie within 200 meters of the boundary of a river or lake.

Article 12 (Target Water Quality for Each River Basin Section)
(1) Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment intends to set target water quality for each river basin section under the main clause of Article 9 (1) of the Act, the Minister shall set the targets so that the water quality of major water supply sources can achieve and maintain at least the Slightly Good grade under items 3 (a) 2) and 3 (b) 2) of attached Table 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy. <Amended on July 20, 2012; Oct. 1, 2025; July 28, 2026>
(2) Public notification under the main clause of Article 9 (1) of the Act shall include the following:
1. River basin sections for which target water quality is to be set and the catchment areas affecting them (hereinafter referred to as "catchments");
2. Target water quality at Metropolitan City/Do boundary points;
3. Target water quality for each river basin section.
(3) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall designate the downstream end of a catchment as the target water quality point and measure and ascertain water quality changes in that catchment as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 12-2 (Setting Target Water Quality within Jurisdictions)
(1) Before making public notification under the main clause of Article 9 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall notify Metropolitan City Mayors and Do Governors (hereinafter referred to as "Mayors/Do Governors") of the deadline by which they may notify the Minister, under the proviso of Article 9 (1) of the Act, of their intention to set target water quality for each river basin section within their jurisdictions (hereinafter referred to as "jurisdictional target water quality") and the deadline by which they may apply to the Minister for approval. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(2) Where a Mayor/Do Governor intends to publicly announce jurisdictional target water quality under the proviso of Article 9 (1) of the Act, the Mayor/Do Governor shall notify the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment of the intention to set such target water quality within the notification period under paragraph (1), and shall then apply to the Minister for approval of the jurisdictional target water quality within the application period under paragraph (1). <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) The criteria for approval under the proviso of Article 9 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. The jurisdictional target water quality shall be appropriately set so that the target water quality at Metropolitan City/Do boundary points publicly notified by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under the proviso of Article 9 (1) of the Act can be achieved and maintained;
2. The jurisdictional target water quality shall be set on the basis of an appropriate analysis of any of the following:
(a) Current water use and flow rates for each catchment;
(b) Current natural and geographical pollution sources within the catchment, etc. and projections of pollution sources;
(c) Quantities of pollutants generated and discharged by each pollution source within the catchment, etc.;
(d) The relationship between water quality and pollution sources.
(4) Where a Mayor/Do Governor has obtained approval under the proviso of Article 9 (1) of the Act, the Mayor/Do Governor shall publicly announce the approved jurisdictional target water quality without delay.
(5) Where a Mayor/Do Governor who has notified an intention to set jurisdictional target water quality under paragraph (1) falls under any of the following, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall, without delay, set and publicly notify target water quality for each river basin section in the relevant area: <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Where the Mayor/Do Governor fails to apply for approval within the application period under paragraph (1), or applies but fails to obtain approval;
2. Where the Mayor/Do Governor fails to make the public announcement under paragraph (4).

Article 13 (Jurisdiction over Business Places)
"Business places prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the former part of the main sentence of Article 12 (1) of the Act means the business places specified in attached Table 1-2. <Amended on July 28, 2014>

Article 14 (Methods and Standards for Calculation of Total Pollution Load Excess Penalty Surcharges)
(1) The method for calculating gains from excess discharges, imposition coefficients by excess rate, area, and number of violations under Article 13 (3) of the Act, and the method for calculating total pollution load excess penalty surcharges under Article 13 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "total pollution load excess penalty surcharges") shall be as specified in attached Table 2. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(2) The number of violations under paragraph (1) shall be the number of orders to take measures, orders to suspend operations, or closure orders received under Article 12 (6) and (8) of the Act. In such cases, the number of violations shall be calculated for each business place for the most recent two-year period as of the date of the violation. <Amended on July 28, 2014>

Article 15 (Notice of Payment of Total Pollution Load Excess Penalty Surcharges)
(1) Notice of payment of a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge shall be given within 60 days from the date the grounds for imposition arise. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(2) Notice of payment of a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge shall be given in writing, stating the quantity of pollutants subject to imposition, the amount imposed, the payment period and place, and other necessary matters. In such cases, the payment period for the surcharge shall be 30 days from the date the payment notice is issued. <Amended on July 12, 2016>

Article 16 (Adjustment of Total Pollution Load Excess Penalty Surcharges)
(1) In any of the following cases, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, a Metropolitan City Mayor, or the head of a Si/Gun (hereinafter referred to as the "imposing authority") shall recalculate and adjust the total pollution load excess penalty surcharge; where there is a difference between the amount already paid and the adjusted amount, the difference shall be additionally imposed or refunded: <Amended on July 28, 2014; July 12, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Where implementation of measures or an order is not completed by the scheduled completion date under an order to take measures, an order to suspend operations, or a closure order under Article 12 (6) or (8) of the Act, or is completed within that period, thereby changing the discharge period of pollutants or discharged substances on which calculation of the surcharge is based;
2. Where, after imposition of the surcharge, discharge conditions of pollutants, etc. are considered to have changed from those at the initial measurement due to improvements to facilities or other reasons, and a subsequent inspection reveals that the quantity of pollutants or discharged substances differs from the quantity initially measured.
(2) Where adjusting a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge on grounds under paragraph (1) 1, the discharge period of pollutants or discharged substances for calculating the surcharge shall be calculated by reflecting the difference between the scheduled completion date and the actual completion date. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) Where adjusting a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge on grounds under paragraph (1) 2, the surcharge shall be recalculated on the basis of the remeasured quantity of pollutants or discharged substances, limited to the period after the date of the subsequent inspection. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(4) Adjusted imposition or refund of a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge under paragraph (1) 1 shall be made within 30 days from the date compliance with completion of improvements, suspension of operations, or completion of closure of the relevant discharge facilities or prevention facilities is confirmed. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(5) Where the imposing authority adjusts a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge and additionally imposes or refunds the difference, it shall give written notice stating the amount, reasons, place of payment or refund, and other necessary matters. <Amended on July 12, 2016>

Article 17 (Applications for Adjustment of Total Pollution Load Excess Penalty Surcharges)
(1) A business operator who receives a notice of payment of a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge (hereinafter referred to as a "person liable for payment") may apply for adjustment of the surcharge where grounds falling under any subparagraph of Article 16 (1) exist. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(2) An application for adjustment under paragraph (1) shall be filed within 30 days from the date the notice of payment of the total pollution load excess penalty surcharge is received. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) Where an application for adjustment is filed, the imposing authority shall notify the applicant of the result within 30 days.

Article 18 (Extension of Payment Deadlines and Installment Payment of Total Pollution Load Excess Penalty Surcharges)
(1) The imposing authority may extend the deadline for payment of a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge or allow payment in installments under the proviso of Article 29 of the General Act on Public Administration; the same shall apply to amounts in arrears. In such cases, extension of the payment deadline shall not exceed one year from the day following the payment deadline, and installment payments shall be limited to six installments within a period of 12 months.
(2) Where a total pollution load excess penalty surcharge payable by a person granted an extension or installment payment under paragraph (1) exceeds twice the person's capital or total contributions (total assets in the case of an individual business operator), and the imposing authority considers that the person remains unable to pay within the period under paragraph (1) because grounds falling under any subparagraph of Article 29 of the General Act on Public Administration continue to exist, the imposing authority may grant a further extension or allow further installment payments.
(3) An extension under paragraph (2) shall not exceed three years from the day following the deadline extended under paragraph (1), and installment payments shall be limited to 12 installments within a period of 36 months.

Article 19 (Payment of Collection Expenses)
(1) Pursuant to Article 13 (7) of the Act, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall pay Metropolitan City Mayors and heads of Sis/Guns, as collection expenses, an amount equivalent to 10 percent of the total pollution load excess penalty surcharges and additional charges they have collected (where adjusted under Article 16, the adjusted surcharges and additional charges). <Amended on July 12, 2016; Oct. 1, 2025>
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall settle each month the collection expenses under paragraph (1) from among total pollution load excess penalty surcharges and additional charges paid into the Special Account for Environmental Improvement under Article 45 of the Framework Act on Environmental Policy and shall pay them to the relevant Metropolitan City Mayors and heads of Sis/Guns by the following month. <Amended on July 12, 2016; Mar. 9, 2021; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 20 (Scope of Buildings and Other Facilities for Which Permission, etc. Is Prohibited upon Noncompliance with Total Pollution Load Management)
"Buildings and other facilities of at least a size prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 16 (1) 4 of the Act means buildings and other facilities under Article 8.

Article 20-2 (Expenses Necessary for Total Pollution Load Management)
"Expenses necessary for total pollution load management prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 17 of the Act means the following expenses: <Amended on May 9, 2014; July 28, 2014; July 12, 2016>
1. Expenses necessary to formulate master plans and implementation plans for total pollution load management under Articles 10 and 11 of the Act;
2. Expenses necessary for evaluations under Article 11 (4) of the Act.

Article 20-3 Deleted. <Mar. 9, 2021>

Article 21 (Scope of Areas Surrounding Dams, etc.)
(1) "Areas surrounding dams prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 23 (1) 2 of the Act means areas within five kilometers of a dam falling under any of the following subparagraphs; provided, for a city area under subparagraph 5 of Article 30 [limited to a city area containing one multipurpose dam under subparagraph 2 of Article 2 of the Act on Dam Construction and Management and Assistance to Their Environs (hereinafter referred to as a "multipurpose dam")], areas downstream of the dam shall be excluded. <Amended on July 21, 2020; Apr. 25, 2023>
1. A dam with a reservoir surface area of at least two million square meters;
2. A dam with a total storage capacity of at least 20 million cubic meters.
(2) "Within the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 23 (1) 3 of the Act means within the standards specified in the following subparagraphs:
1. For an area whose annual average biochemical oxygen demand exceeded 10 milligrams per liter: An annual average biochemical oxygen demand no more than one-fifth of that before residents' voluntary efforts or no more than 3.3 milligrams per liter;
2. For an area whose annual average biochemical oxygen demand had remained at no more than 10 milligrams per liter: An annual average biochemical oxygen demand no more than one-third of that before residents' voluntary efforts or no more than one milligram per liter.
(3) Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu (the head of a Gu meaning the head of an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply) considers that an area under Article 23 (1) 3 of the Act exists within the jurisdiction, the head shall submit the following materials concerning that area to the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment by March 31 each year: <Amended on June 30, 2009; Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Water quality data measured by any of the following testing institutions:
(a) The National Institute of Environmental Research and its affiliated institutions;
(b) Health and environment research institutes of Metropolitan Cities and Dos;
(c) River basin environmental offices and regional environmental offices;
(d) Offices of the Korea Environment Corporation under the Korea Environment Corporation Act;
(e) Other water quality testing institutions recognized by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment;
2. The size of the relevant area and the status of its residents;
3. Methods and details of water quality improvement;
4. Details of local residents' activities to improve water quality.

Article 22 (Scope of Eligibility for Resident Support Projects)
(1) The scope of residents or areas eligible for support through resident support projects under Article 23 (1) of the Act shall be as follows: <Amended on May 9, 2014; July 28, 2014>
1. Residents of water source management areas who have met both of the following requirements since before designation of the area as a water source management area, and the villages in which those residents reside:
(a) They shall have continuously maintained resident registration and actually resided in the Si/Gun/Gu (in the case of a Gu, an autonomous Gu; hereinafter the same shall apply) having jurisdiction over a riparian zone under Article 4 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "riparian zone") or a water source protection area under Article 7 (1) of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act and Article 7 (1) of this Act (hereinafter referred to as a "water source protection area") [including a case of moving out for unavoidable reasons, such as education, medical treatment, or official duties, and moving back within six months (limited to one occasion)];
(b) They shall have continuously owned land, etc. in the riparian zone or water source protection area;
2. Residents who are spouses or lineal ascendants or descendants who inherit, or receive as a gift in its entirety, land, etc. continuously owned in the area since before designation of the riparian zone or water source protection area by a resident under subparagraph 1, and who have continuously maintained resident registration and actually resided in the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over the relevant zone or area since before the inheritance or gift [including a case of moving out after the inheritance or gift for unavoidable reasons, such as education, medical treatment, or official duties, and moving back within six months (limited to one occasion)], and the villages in which those residents reside;
3. Residents of water source management areas who do not fall under subparagraph 1 or 2 and who have continuously resided in the relevant water source protection area since before its designation;
4. Residents of water source management areas who do not fall under subparagraphs 1 through 3 and who have continuously engaged in livelihoods prescribed by the Committee, such as agriculture, forestry, or fisheries, in the relevant water source protection area since before its designation;
5. Residents who have continuously maintained resident registration and actually resided in the Si/Gun/Gu having jurisdiction over an area surrounding a dam under Article 21 (1) (hereinafter referred to as an "area surrounding a dam") since before construction of the dam, and who have continuously owned land, etc. in that area surrounding the dam;
6. Water source management areas, areas surrounding dams, and areas under Article 23 (1) 3 of the Act;
7. Areas of Sis/Guns/Gus having jurisdiction over areas under Article 23 (1) 4 or 5 of the Act.
(2) In applying paragraph (1) 1 or 2, where land, etc. is jointly owned, only one co-owner shall be deemed the owner (selected by agreement among the parties or, where no agreement is reached, the owner with the largest share; where multiple owners have the largest share, one person selected according to criteria prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment). <Amended on May 9, 2014; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 23 (Criteria for Allocation of Support Funds, etc.)
(1) Resident support projects under Article 23 (1) of the Act shall be classified as indirect support projects, direct support projects, and special support projects, the details of which shall be as specified in attached Table 3. <Amended on July 28, 2014>
(2) The persons eligible for resident support projects under paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "resident support project beneficiaries") and the applicable criteria for each target area shall be as specified in attached Table 4. <Amended on June 30, 2009; July 28, 2014>
(3) Financial resources provided for resident support projects (hereinafter referred to as "resident support project funds") shall be classified as funds used for indirect and direct support projects (hereinafter referred to as "general support project funds") and funds used for special support projects (hereinafter referred to as "special support project funds"). <Amended on July 28, 2014>
(4) The Committee shall determine and allocate the areas eligible for and amounts of special support project funds, taking into account the extent of installation of resident convenience facilities and pollutant purification facilities, the status of renewable energy deployment, etc.; the portion of special support project funds used for water quality improvement and regional development projects under item 3 (b) of attached Table 3 shall not exceed the amount calculated by the following formula: <Amended on July 28, 2026>

(Annual resident support project funds ? Funds used for projects to install and operate renewable energy facilities under item 3 (a) of attached Table 3) × 30%

(5) General support project funds shall consist of resident support project funds excluding special support project funds. In such cases, an amount equivalent to 50 percent of the general support project funds shall be allocated in consideration of land area in each water source management area within the Sis/Guns/Gus having jurisdiction over the residences of resident support project beneficiaries and weights prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment according to restrictions on activities; the remainder shall be allocated in consideration of the degree of support per beneficiary. Detailed allocation methods shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on June 30, 2009; July 28, 2014; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 24 (Procedures for Implementing Resident Support Projects, etc.)
(1) To facilitate implementation of resident support projects under Article 23 of the Act, the Committee shall notify the heads of Sis/Guns/Gus having jurisdiction over the residences of resident support project beneficiaries of the following by March 31 each year: <Amended on June 30, 2009; Mar. 9, 2021>
1. The amount of resident support project funds for the following year from the Nakdong River Basin Management Fund under Article 33 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund");
2. Guidelines for formulating the following year's resident support project plan (hereinafter referred to as the "project plan").
(2) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall formulate a project plan including the following in accordance with the project plan formulation guidelines under paragraph (1), obtain approval from the competent Mayor/Do Governor, and submit it to the Committee by April 30:
1. An implementation plan for the detailed content of resident support projects in attached Table 3;
2. Other matters prescribed in the project plan formulation guidelines.
(3) Where formulating a project plan under paragraph (2), the head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall gather residents' opinions according to the procedures and methods prescribed by ordinance of the relevant Si/Gun/Gu; provided, this shall not apply to a project for which consent of the Si/Gun/Gu council has been obtained as prescribed by ordinance of the relevant Si/Gun/Gu.
(4) The Committee shall deliberate on the project plan in consideration of the proposed fund management plan under Article 66 (5) of the National Finance Act and notify the head of the Si/Gun/Gu of the results without delay.
(5) Where the head of a Si/Gun/Gu intends to change important matters, such as project scale or resident support project funds, in a project plan deliberated on by the Committee, the head shall obtain approval from the competent Mayor/Do Governor and have the Committee deliberate on it again. In such cases, important changes requiring renewed deliberation by the Committee shall be prescribed in the project plan formulation guidelines under paragraph (1).
(6) The head of a Si/Gun/Gu shall submit the results of resident support projects for each year to the Committee by March 31 of the following year.

Article 24-2 (Management of Real Estate Acquired through Resident Support Projects)
(1) "Village associations and other resident communities prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 23-2 (1) of the Act means resident communities, such as village associations, that are unincorporated associations composed of all or some residents of administrative areas such as Dongs or Ris (hereinafter referred to as "resident communities").

Without the consent of the competent head of the Si/Gun/Gu, the land or building may not be transferred, limited real rights may not be created over it, and no act restricting ownership, including attachment, provisional attachment, or provisional disposition, may be carried out."

Article 25 (Standards for Support to Business Places, etc.)
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies may give priority in technical and financial support under Article 24 of the Act to small or medium enterprise operators (meaning small or medium enterprise operators under subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion Act) who intend to improve any of the following facilities: <Amended on Nov. 20, 2009; Jan. 16, 2018; Oct. 1, 2025>
1. Water pollution prevention facilities under subparagraph 12 of Article 2 of the Water Environment Conservation Act;
2. Treatment facilities under subparagraph 8 of Article 2 of the Act on the Management and Use of Livestock Excreta.

Article 26 (Support for Operation of Water Pollution Prevention Facilities)
(1) The Committee may provide support within 30 percent of the operating expenses of water pollution prevention facilities under Article 25 of the Act.
(2) A person intending to receive support under Article 25 of the Act shall apply to the Committee by March 31 each year as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 27 (Notification, etc.)
Where the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment, a Metropolitan City Mayor, or the head of a Si/Gun intends to give notification under Article 27 (2) of the Act, it shall be made in a document containing the principal details of the project plan and a list of land, etc. to be used or expropriated. <Amended on July 28, 2014; Oct. 1, 2025>

Article 28 (Scope of Public Waters Subject to Water Use Charges)
"Public waters prescribed by Presidential Decree" in the main clause of Article 32 (1) and the main sentence of Article 32 (2) of the Act means the following waters: <Amended on June 14, 2022; Apr. 25, 2023>
1. The mainstream of the Nakdong River;
2. Dams in the Nakdong River basin whose stored water is used as a regional water supply source under subparagraph 3 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act;
3. Multipurpose dams in the Nakdong River basin;
4. River sections from dams under subparagraph 2 or 3 to the mainstream of the Nakdong River;
5. Sections designated by the Committee in which water that has seeped underground or elsewhere from waters under subparagraphs 1 through 4 and is flowing or stagnant is withdrawn.

Article 29 (Submission of Materials)
(1) Pursuant to Article 32 (4) of the Act, a waterworks business operator shall submit materials containing the following to the Committee by the 15th day of the month following the month in which notice of payment of water use charges under Article 32 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "water use charges") is given:
1. Quantity of raw water withdrawn;
2. Quantity of tap water supplied and the loss rate;
3. Calculation data and payment details for water use charges;
4. Other materials requested by the chairperson of the Committee as deemed necessary for calculating and forecasting water use charges.
(2) Where the head of a Si/Gun authorizes installation of a private water supply system or private industrial water supply system under Articles 52 and 54 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act in waters under Article 28, the head shall notify the Committee thereof without delay.
(3) Where the head of the flood control office having jurisdiction over the Nakdong River basin grants permission to use river water under Article 50 of the River Act, the head shall notify the Committee thereof without delay.
(4) Where the Korea Water Resources Corporation under the Korea Water Resources Corporation Act concludes a contract with a local government to supply raw water withdrawn from public waters subject to water use charges under Article 28, either directly or after treatment, it shall notify the Committee of its details without delay. <Added on July 12, 2016>

Article 30 (Areas Exempt from Water Use Charges)
"Areas prescribed by Presidential Decree" in Article 32 (5) of the Act means the following areas: <Amended on July 12, 2016; July 21, 2020>
1. Water source management areas;
2. Areas falling under the main clause of Article 21 (1);
3. Areas of Sis/Guns in which at least two multipurpose dams are located;
4. Catchment areas of rivers flowing into multipurpose dams (meaning areas in which rainwater naturally flows into rivers, lakes, or other public waters and which are enclosed by lines connecting the surrounding ridges);
5. City areas in which more than half of the Dongs are included in areas falling under subparagraph 2.

Article 31 (Determination and Public Notification of Rates of Water Use Charges)
(1) The Committee shall deliberate on and adjust the rates of water use charges under Article 32 (1) and (2) of the Act every two years, taking into account the financial resources required for the purposes of the Fund under Article 35 of the Act.
(2) The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall publicly notify the rates of water use charges deliberated on and adjusted under paragraph (1) no later than 90 days before the beginning of the fiscal year. <Amended on Oct. 1, 2025>
(3) Where rates have not been publicly notified under paragraph (2), the most recently publicly notified rates shall apply.

Article 32 (Method of Calculating End Users' Water Consumption)
(1) An end user's water consumption under Article 32 (1) of the Act shall be the water consumption used as the basis for imposing and collecting water charges.
(2) Where a waterworks business operator supplies a mixture of water from public waters subject to water use charges under Article 28 and water from other public waters, notwithstanding paragraph (1), the water consumption calculated by multiplying the water consumption under subparagraph 1 by the ratio under subparagraph 2 shall be the end user's water consumption in the water supply area under that operator's jurisdiction (where the waterworks business operator is a local government, the jurisdiction of that local government): <Amended on July 12, 2016>
1. Water consumption used as the basis for imposing and collecting water charges;
2. The ratio of the quantity of water from public waters subject to water use charges to the total quantity of water supplied by the relevant waterworks business operator in the preceding year (where there was no supply from public waters subject to water use charges in the preceding year, the planned quantity to be supplied in the relevant year).

Article 33 (Calculation, Imposition, and Collection of Water Use Charges for End Users)
(1) Water use charges for end users under Article 32 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "water use charges for end users") shall be calculated by multiplying the rate under Article 31 by the water consumption under Article 32.
(2) Water use charges for end users shall be imposed together with the water charge payment notice and collected in cash or by credit card, debit card, or similar means (hereinafter referred to as "credit cards, etc."). <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) A waterworks business operator shall pay into the Fund without delay the water use charges imposed on and collected from end users.
(4) Except as provided in this Decree, detailed methods and procedures for imposing and collecting water use charges for end users, etc. shall follow the procedures for collecting water charges prescribed by ordinance of the relevant local government; provided, where the waterworks business operator is not a local government, the procedures for collecting water charges prescribed in the supply regulations under Article 38 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act shall apply.

Article 34 (Water Use Charges for Installers of Private Water Supply Systems and River Water Users, etc.)
(1) Water use charges for installers of private water supply systems and river water users under Article 32 (2) of the Act shall be calculated by multiplying the quantity of water withdrawn by the relevant installer or river water user by the rate under Article 31; where the quantity withdrawn by an installer of a private water supply system is unknown, the charges shall be calculated on the basis of the average daily water supply under Article 58 (2) 3 of the Enforcement Decree of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act.
(2) Installers of private water supply systems and river water users shall notify the Committee of the quantity of water withdrawn each month and the corresponding water use charges by the 10th day of the following month and shall pay the charges into the Fund in cash or by credit cards, etc. by the last day of the following month. <Amended on July 12, 2016>
(3) The Committee shall conclude agreements with credit card business operators under subparagraph 2-2 of Article 2 of the Specialized Credit Finance Business Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as "payment processing agencies") to enable payment of water use charges by credit cards, etc. <Added on July 12, 2016>
(4) Where water use charges are paid by credit cards, etc. under paragraph (2), the date of approval by the payment processing agency shall be deemed the payment date. <Added on July 12, 2016>

Article 34-2 (Exemption from Water Use Charges for River Water Users)
Where a river water user under Article 32 (2) 2 of the Act falls under any of the following, water use charges shall be exempted under paragraph (7) of that Article: <Amended on Jan. 16, 2018; Mar. 9, 2021>
1. Where the State or a local government uses river water to measure water pollution;
2. Where river water is used for any of the following purposes, no water pollutants under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Water Environment Conservation Act are newly contained in the water discharged into the river after use, and there is no difference between the quantity of river water withdrawn and the quantity discharged:
(a) Where an electricity generation business operator under subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Electric Utility Act uses river water as cooling water;
(b) Where river water is used to produce hydrothermal energy under Article 2 (4) and item 5 of attached Table 1 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy.

Article 35 (Entrustment of Compulsory Collection)
A waterworks business operator intending to entrust compulsory collection of water use charges under Article 32 (9) of the Act shall send a document stating the following to the head of the local government to which the collection is to be entrusted:
1. Name and address of the person liable for payment;
2. Amount payable and payment deadline;
3. Whether a reminder or final demand for payment has been issued and the date of its issuance;
4. Other necessary matters.

Article 36 (Purposes of the Fund)
"Projects or expenses prescribed by Presidential Decree" in subparagraph 16 of Article 35 of the Act means the following projects or expenses: <Amended on June 30, 2009; Jan. 16, 2018; Jan. 8, 2019; July 21, 2020; Mar. 9, 2021; Feb. 13, 2024>
1. Projects to create riparian green spaces;
2. Support for operating expenses of buffer storage facilities installed in industrial complexes developed on or before July 14, 2002 (including industrial complexes for which sale announcements were made), and industrial areas designated on or before June 30, 2009;
3. Education and publicity for water quality improvement;
3-2. Maintenance and management projects for water intake and treatment facilities among waterworks facilities under subparagraph 17 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act;
4. Support for water treatment expenses of general waterworks business operators under subparagraph 22 of Article 3 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act (meaning persons withdrawing water from public waters subject to water use charges under Article 28) in any of the following cases:
(a) Where the monthly average biochemical oxygen demand of raw water exceeds three milligrams per liter;
(b) Where an algae alert has been issued for the raw water;
(c) Where the sum of the monthly average concentrations of perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) and perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) in raw water exceeds 0.07 micrograms per liter;
(d) Where the monthly average concentration of perfluorohexane sulfonic acid (PFHxS) in raw water exceeds 0.48 micrograms per liter;
(e) Where the monthly average total organic carbon in raw water exceeds four milligrams per liter;
5. Support for local governments supplying regional water supply systems (limited to supply of water stored in dams);
6. Forestry projects to enhance water source replenishment functions;
7. Management of water source management areas;
8. Basic environmental survey projects;
9. Management of purchased land, etc.;
10. Nonpoint pollution reduction projects;
11. Expenses for transporting and treating waste under Article 31 (1) of the Water Environment Conservation Act (limited to expenses recognized by the Committee from among the portions borne by local governments for waste arising at dams designated by the Committee);
12. Survey and research projects on the current use of water resources, including river water;
13. Projects to survey and manage leaked or abandoned livestock excreta, compost, and liquid fertilizer;
14. Projects to prevent and reduce algae occurrence;
15. Other projects or expenses selected by the Committee for water management in the Nakdong River basin.

Article 37 (Operation and Management of the Fund)
(1) Where a fund management plan has been finalized under Article 66 of the National Finance Act, the Committee shall notify the relevant local governments thereof.
(2) The Committee shall examine and evaluate the execution and use of Fund support received by local governments, etc. and reflect the results in the following year's fund management plan.
